excerpt: Vivodyne grows lab-made human tissues in robotic labs to test drugs before clinical trials. Funding from Khosla Ventures, what it does and alternatives.
content:
Vivodyne is a biotech company that grows human organ tissues in the lab and tests drug candidates on them, as an alternative to animal studies before human clinical trials. Its tissues grow on microfluidic chips it calls TissueDisks; robotic labs it calls HIVEs cultivate, dose and analyse thousands of tissues at a time and generate imaging, single-cell sequencing and protein data. Its website says each HIVE tests 10,000 human tissues at a time and that the data is used to train AI models of human biology. It works with pharmaceutical partners rather than selling a product to the public.

Andrei Georgescu is cofounder and CEO. In November 2023 Vivodyne announced a $38 million seed round led by Khosla Ventures, with CS Ventures, Bison Ventures, MBX Capital and Kairos Ventures; Pharmaceutical Technology reported that it had bio-engineered more than 20 human organ tissue types. In May 2025 it announced a $40 million Series A, again led by Khosla Ventures, with Lingotto Investment Management, Helena Capital and Fortius Ventures joining. STAT tied the raise to the FDA and NIH moving away from animal testing requirements. The company said it would open a 23,000-square-foot robotic lab in South San Francisco.

Vivodyne does not publish prices; drug developers contact it to set up a partnership. Its customers are pharmaceutical and biotech companies that want human data earlier in a drug programme; it is not a product individual researchers can buy off the shelf. Rivals such as Emulate and CN Bio sell organ-on-chip systems that labs run themselves.

We have not used Vivodyne for this page. It brings together Vivodyne's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
